gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch (33 files, ~6300 lines) addresses all stated requirements: (1) atomic persistence via new persist_accepted_note_snapshot combining content/search/graph writes, (2) separate persist_accepted_note_move preserving existing graph, (3) module relocation from basic_memory.cloud.* to basic_memory.services.* and basic_memory.index.*, (4) architecture boundary enforcement, (5) project delete acceptance moved to services. The patch is comprehensive and coherent with the issue description.
base_vs_gold_expectation: Tests would fail on the unpatched base due to: (1) missing modules basic_memory.services.{directory_deletes,note_content_reads,note_content_writes,note_preparation,project_deletes}, (2) missing basic_memory.index.note_content_materialization, (3) missing functions persist_accepted_note_snapshot and persist_accepted_note_move, (4) cloud imports in core modules violating architecture boundary test, (5) repository importing indexing modules. Tests should pass after gold patch. Good discrimination between base and gold.
too_narrow_risks: No test for project delete acceptance (the issue mentions runtime-neutral project delete orchestration with specific error messages for missing/inactive projects and default project protection, but no test in eval covers this behavior)
No test for the move operation's graph preservation semantics at the API/route level (only tested at the unit level via persist_accepted_note_move which just checks it doesn't call graph repos)
No test for the 'notes with no observations or relations must still clear the existing graph by replacing with empty sets' requirement at the integration/API level

No test for compatibility imports — the issue says 'Existing compatibility imports from basic_memory.cloud.directory_deletes and basic_memory.cloud.note_content_materialization should continue to work for downstream users' but no test verifies the shims actually re-export correctly
too_broad_risks: The eval runs 11 test files with many pre-existing tests (50+ tests total) that go beyond the specific issue requirements — failures in unrelated pre-existing tests would reject valid solutions

Architecture boundary tests (test_architecture_boundaries.py) enforce a very specific module layout that constrains alternative valid implementations — a solution that achieves atomicity and correct move semantics but organizes modules differently would fail
implementation_coupling: Test patch imports from specific new module paths (basic_memory.services.note_preparation.PreparedEntityWrite/PreparedEntityFields/PreparedEntityMove) — alternative naming or location would fail
Test patch imports persist_accepted_note_snapshot and persist_accepted_note_move by exact name from basic_memory.indexing.accepted_note_write_runner — alternative function names would fail

persistence_calls fixture monkeypatches specific function references (accepted_note_mutation_module.persist_accepted_note_snapshot/persist_accepted_note_move) — this checks implementation dispatch, not observable behavior

Test patch changes existing test type annotations from local _PreparedWrite/_PreparedFields/_PreparedMove to imported PreparedEntityWrite/PreparedEntityFields/PreparedEntityMove — forces specific type names in specific modules
Import path changes in 9 existing test files (cloud.* → services.* or index.*) are coupled to the gold patch's specific module relocation strategy
environment_risks: uv binary is at /opt/venv/bin/uv which is covered by the PATH setup in eval.sh, but uv is not on the default system PATH — if the PATH loop fails to execute, uv would not be found
The test command uses 'uv run $PYTHON -m pytest' which requires uv to manage the project environment correctly — if uv's project resolution fails, all tests fail regardless of code quality
BASIC_MEMORY_ENV=test environment variable must be set correctly for test database configuration
mismatches: The issue mentions project delete acceptance with specific error messages (404 for missing/inactive, 400 for default project) but the test patch only changes an import path in test_project_deletes.py without adding tests for these specific behaviors

The issue says 'move operations are different: changing a note path must not replace or clear its observations and relations' — while test_persist_accepted_note_move_is_explicitly_content_and_search_only verifies the move doesn't touch graph repos, there's no test that positively verifies observations/relations survive a move
Task is categorized as 'debugging' in task.toml but the issue is actually a large-scale refactoring/architectural task

evidence.detail: 1196-line test patch modifying 11 test files, 2 new test files (test_accepted_note_atomicity.py, test_architecture_boundaries.py), rest are import path changes and type renaming
6342-line solve script containing a 33-file gold patch — very large refactoring scope
Runs 11 test files with -x flag (stop on first failure), marker exclusions for postgres/semantic/live
Base has persist_accepted_note_write and replace_accepted_note_graph as separate functions; gold replaces with persist_accepted_note_snapshot (combined) and persist_accepted_note_move
test_architecture_boundaries.py uses AST-based static analysis to enforce module dependency direction — tests the refactoring structure, not runtime behavior
Cloud modules exist in base and contain full implementations; gold reduces them to compatibility shims

summary: Large refactoring instance (33 files changed) with tests that have strong implementation coupling. The core atomicity test (test_accepted_note_atomicity.py) and architecture boundary test (test_architecture_boundaries.py) are well-designed for the stated requirements and correctly discriminate base from gold. However, the test patch is heavily coupled to the gold solution's specific module layout (basic_memory.services.* and basic_memory.index.*), specific type names (PreparedEntityWrite/Fields/Move), and specific function names (persist_accepted_note_snapshot/move). Alternative valid implementations that achieve the same behavioral goals with different module organization would fail. Several issue requirements (project delete acceptance errors, compatibility shim verification, positive graph-preservation for moves) lack test coverage. The eval also runs many pre-existing tests that could cause spurious failures unrelated to the core changes.
